title: Are Google Local Services Ads Worth It? (2026)
desc: Are Google Local Services Ads worth it for contractors? What LSA leads cost in 2026, how disputes work, LSA vs Google Ads, and the free fixes to make first.

blocks.h1: Are Local Services Ads worth it? *Fix three free things first.*
blocks.lede: For many contractors in the USA and Canada, Google Local Services Ads are one of the better paid options: you pay per lead, not per click, and the ad sits at the very top of the search. But they work far better when your free Google presence is already strong. Fix those first, then test a small budget and track booked jobs.
ticks: The three free fixes that make ads cheaper

blocks.html:
Are Google Local Services Ads worth it?

Often, yes, for contractors who answer the phone quickly and have good reviews. Local Services Ads charge when a customer calls, messages or books you through the ad, not when someone clicks. The lead also comes to you alone, which is a big difference from shared lead platforms.

They are a poor fit if your calls go to voicemail, your reviews are thin, or your profile is half finished, because Google ranks and prices ads partly on profile quality.

How much do Local Services Ads cost in 2026?

Google does not publish a fixed price. You pay per valid lead and the price changes with your trade, your area and the time of year.

  • A February 2026 industry benchmark across 888 contractors put the average home services lead at about $53, with general contractors much higher.
  • The same data showed roughly 44% of leads booking, which works out to about $233 per paying customer.
  • Bad leads (spam, wrong service, outside your area) can be disputed. Google's help pages say credit requests are not considered after 30 days, so check your leads weekly.

Google is also moving Local Services Ads into Google Ads as a pay per lead campaign type during 2026. The pay per lead model stays, but the settings look different.

Local Services Ads vs regular Google Ads

Local Services AdsGoogle Search Ads
You pay forA call, message or bookingA click
Where it showsTop of local searchSearch results and more
Needs a website?No, but reviews and profile matterYes, a page that converts
Small budgetWorkableHard; clicks add up fast

Contractors in forums give the same advice about regular ads: a few hundred dollars spread across every service and town gets almost nothing. Narrow it to one service in a handful of towns, send people to a page about that service, and judge it on booked jobs, not clicks.

Three free things to fix before you spend $1

  1. Your Google Business Profile. Right category, every service, real photos, service areas and hours. Use our checklist.
  2. Your reviews. A steady flow of recent reviews makes every ad and every free listing work harder. Text a review link the day a job finishes.
  3. Where people land. If an ad or a listing sends people to a slow, vague homepage, they leave. A fast page for each service with a tap to call button keeps them. See what a trade website needs.

How to test Local Services Ads properly

  • Start with one or two services you most want more of.
  • Answer every call live during working hours. Missed calls are paid for and wasted.
  • Dispute invalid leads every week.
  • After a month, divide what you spent by the jobs you booked. That is the only number that matters.

How Google decides who shows first

Paying more is not the only lever. Google says ranking and lead cost in Local Services Ads depend on things like your distance to the customer, your reviews and rating, how responsive you are, your business hours and how complete your profile is. In practice that means:

  • Reviews matter twice: once in the ad itself and again in where you rank.
  • Missed calls hurt. Answering quickly helps you rank and stops you paying for leads you never speak to.
  • Set your hours honestly. Ads show when you say you are open, so make sure someone answers then.

Verification and badges

To run Local Services Ads, Google checks your business, usually including licence and insurance details for many trades, and in some cases background checks. Once verified you get a badge on your ad, which builds trust before the customer even calls. Have your paperwork ready before you start; verification can take a while.

When Local Services Ads are not worth it

  • You cannot answer the phone during the day.
  • Your average job is small and your area is very competitive.
  • You already have more work than you can handle from Google and referrals.
  • Your profile has very few reviews; build those first.

blocks.title: Your checklist.
items: Complete every field of your Google Business Profile
Get at least a few recent Google reviews
Make sure each main service has its own web page
Start Local Services Ads on one or two services only
Track booked jobs, not leads or clicks
Review cost per booked job after a month

items.q: Do you pay per click with Local Services Ads?
items.a: No. You pay when a customer contacts you through the ad by calling, messaging or booking. Clicks that never contact you cost nothing.

items.q: How much is a Local Services Ads lead?
items.a: Google does not publish prices. A 2026 benchmark across hundreds of contractors put the average home services lead at about $53, with big differences by trade and city.

items.q: Can I get money back for bad Local Services leads?
items.a: You can dispute leads that are spam, outside your area or for work you do not do. Google says requests are not considered after 30 days.

items.q: Do I need a website for Local Services Ads?
items.a: Not to run them, but customers often check your website and reviews before they call. A strong site and profile help you win the lead you paid for.

items.q: Is $500 a month enough for Google Ads?
items.a: For regular search ads it is tight. Focus it on one service in a few towns, or start with Local Services Ads where you pay per lead instead of per click.
